analyst_view.overall: Inter (15th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight. Inter drew 4-4 at Atalanta on Sunday after giving up three two-goal leads; Lautaro Martínez came back with a late cameo and is expected to start, but Hakan Çalhanoğlu is now out with a thigh problem from that game (UEFA and Sports Mole; another preview calls him questionable), and Bonny (counted) is out. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke; Stiller (groin, counted out), Jaquez and Sauer are doubts, and Demirović (four Champions League goals) leads the line. French referee François Letexier (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted. Lautaro's return and Çalhanoğlu's absence pull Inter's goals in opposite directions, so I drop my earlier small lift and stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take Bonny off Inter and Stiller off Stuttgart (about -4% each). Lautaro starting adds to Inter's attack, but losing Çalhanoğlu, their penalty and set-piece taker, takes some of that back, and neither is in the numbers. They roughly cancel out, so I drop my earlier +3% and stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.1 corners, 6.2 of them Inter's, already up 6% for Inter's recent corner count. Dimarco and Spence are fit on the flanks and Stuttgart play a wing-back system too, which fits the usual picture, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.7 cards and already take a little off Inter for their quiet recent record and for referee Letexier, who sits near the average at 4.0 a game. Çalhanoğlu, who was one booking from a ban, won't play, and there is no rivalry, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.4 shots and already add about 20% to Inter's side for their recent shooting and take 7% off Stuttgart's. Inter at home with Lautaro and Esposito should shoot plenty, but that is already in the numbers, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, up 7% for Inter's accuracy lately and down 3% for Stuttgart's. Lautaro back sharpens Inter, while Çalhanoğlu's long shots are lost, so I stay at about 10.6.
